description:
Project: Starlight Adventure
Team: Shooting Star

Starlight Adventure is an interactive space exploration game where players experience different roles in a space mission, from astronauts and engineers to scientists and mission controllers. Through exciting challenges, teamwork, and problem-solving, it introduces young minds to space mission design and inspires them to explore STEM careers.
summary:
Starlight Adventure is a old 20's style pixel art mission-control game that turns space-mission design into an adventure kids actually want to play. Players create their own mission ID card name, gender, and profession choosing to be a pilot, engineer, or doctor aboard a station in the year 2026. Every shift follows the real rhythm of a mission: a knowledge quiz that tests mission facts, a profession-specific puzzle shift where engineering decisions matter and a shared arcade finale the whole crew plays together. Choices across the year shape how each mission succeeds, teaching players that a space mission is a web of trade-offs objectives, people, and limited resources not a single correct answer.
I built it because young students are curious about space-tech careers but find career guides boring. Starlight Adventure lets them live a year of missions first and understand the careers behind them after learning by playing, one profession at a time.
details:
What it does / how it works

Starlight Adventure is a night-city mission-control game where a student designs and lives a complete space career, one year at a time. The player starts in 2026 by building their mission ID card name, gender, and profession (pilot, engineer, or doctor) which determines their role on the station. Each shift follows the real rhythm of a mission: a knowledge quiz testing mission facts and procedures, a profession-specific puzzle shift where hands-on decisions and limited time force real trade-offs, and a shared arcade finale the whole crew plays together. Every choice shapes how the year's missions succeed, and a debrief screen reviews what each decision cost or earned exactly how real mission design balances objectives, people, power, and time.

Benefits and intended impact

Career guidance for space technology is usually a wall of text. Starlight Adventure lets students experience the careers first fixing systems as an engineer, managing crew health as a doctor, flying objectives as a pilot and only then understand the profession behind it. The intended impact is early, joyful career discovery: kids finish a year of missions able to say "I know what that job actually feels like." The difficulty is deliberately forgiving so younger players stay motivated, and the game teaches persistence: missions can be retried, and progress is saved between sessions.

Tools and technologies

Built with Godot 4.7 and GDScript, with game content (quizzes, dialogues, puzzles, professions, achievements) driven by JSON data files so missions can be extended without touching code. Original MP3 audio tracks and custom pixel-art assets, a typed boot-sequence intro, and an ID-card profile system. The project is version-controlled on GitHub and deployed as a web export on Vercel, so judges can play instantly in a browser with no install including a tap-to-start screen and a web-specific audio-unlock system for browser sound policies.

Creativity and factors considered

I have used over 50+ personally designed 2d components including backgrounds ,characters and assets , imported an audio package of over 15+ different effect and have designed the dialouges and character personalities to preserve the feeling and the overall immersive experience in the game

The creativity is in the framing: where i have enabled an old asthetic console gaming style for todays children to experience a mission-control seriousness wrapped in a cozy, neon night-city aesthetic, with each mini-game color-coded so puzzles feel like distinct station departments. I considered accessibility (large body text, clear contrast, generous time limits), replayability (shuffled quiz answers, five varied puzzle genres, five future mission years teased as "coming soon"), and authenticity every shift mirrors an actual mission phase, so the fun and the learning are the same activity.
